details:
SfairaX is a web-based visualization tool that makes SPHEREx mission imagery easily accessible. Users can query sky coordinates and receive an interactive timeline of image cutouts. The frontend is deployed on Vercel, while a Python backend handles data retrieval and image processing. It addresses the challenge by providing an easily accessible web tool. This is important as it allows anyone to search through what would be a very tedious and unforgiving dataset.

Detailed Description

SfairaX enables users to generate customized views of SPHEREx data by specifying:

• Cutout size (in arcseconds)

• Right ascension and declination

• Color theme

• Frames per second

• Time range

The tool then displays the requested imagery in a clean, intuitive interface. When live data is unavailable, it falls back to a set of example images so users can still explore the interface and functionality. It offers a user-friendly and simple interface to input parameters and receive data. We hope to achieve a website that anyone can access and explore. Vercel was used for the front end and a Python script is the backend service. The Python script uses Astroquery and Astropy. Throughout the duration of the hackathon, the IRSA services were down almost the entire time, making it difficult to work on the project.

Use of Super Intelligence (SI)

SI was used for drafting and writing minor amounts of code/comments. It was also used for diagnosing deployment bugs and searching documentation. The majority of the work was done by humans. The AI tools used were Google AI Overview and GPT-6 Luna.

NASA Data

We used the NASA IRSA services for retrieving data from the SPHEREx program. We also took inspiration from WiseView and the example Jupyter notebooks. The example images were taken from the SPHEREx Quick Release S3 bucket.
